Your first travel assignment: a checklist

What to settle before you accept, what to pack in your document folder and what to ask on day one.

The first contract is the one with the most unknowns. Most of them disappear if you settle a few things in the right order.

Before you accept

  • Confirm the unit, shift, start date and contract length in writing.
  • Ask about patient ratios, float expectations and the charting system.
  • Check the guaranteed hours and the cancellation terms.
  • Make sure your license for that state is active, or that the timeline is realistic.

Your document folder

  • Licenses and certification cards
  • Immunization records and a recent TB test
  • Two references from recent supervisors
  • Government ID and any documents your agency asks for at onboarding

Housing

Decide early whether you want a stipend or help finding a place. If you are arranging it yourself, book something flexible for the first weeks until you know the commute and the neighbourhood.

The first week

  • Learn where supplies, crash carts and policies live before you need them.
  • Find out who your resource person is on each shift.
  • Tell your recruiter how orientation went, good or bad. They can only fix what they know about.

Around week eight

Start the conversation about what comes next: an extension, a new city or a break. The earlier you say what you want, the more choice you have.
